codex.runtime_consumption_evidence: CONFIRMED for the CLI surface (Codex Cloud's global scope is not independently verified - it keeps its own separate environment/workspace configuration per the official docs, though the project-scope AGENTS.md content EIF manages is part of the repo itself and should behave identically there). Verified 2026-07-17 against `codex --version` (codex-cli 0.144.5) and the official docs (developers.openai.com/codex/guides/agents-md, redirects to learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md). Real runtime proof via `codex debug prompt-input` (no authentication required) against a disposable probe project: confirmed a root AGENTS.md's content is included in the merged instruction chain; confirmed a nested subdirectory's own AGENTS.md is appended after the root's content when cwd is inside it; and - the adapter's central risk - confirmed empirically that an AGENTS.override.md in the SAME directory as AGENTS.md makes the base file's content vanish from the merged chain entirely, not merely add to it. See adapters/codex/README.md for the full evidence trail (sanitized - the raw probe output also captured this machine's own unrelated personal global Codex configuration, which is never reproduced anywhere).
codex.instruction_discovery_model: multi-file CONCATENATION (not first-match) across two independent scopes: global (`$CODEX_HOME`, one file: AGENTS.override.md if present else AGENTS.md) + project (git-root-to-cwd, every matching file found along the walk is joined, not just the closest one). The opposite combination from Hermes (which first-match-selects a single file across scopes that differ per candidate).
codex.precedence: within the project scope: root-to-cwd, ALL matching files concatenated (root first, closest-to-cwd last) - not first-match. Within a single directory: AGENTS.override.md beats AGENTS.md (confirmed empirically: the base file's content vanishes entirely from the merged chain when an override sits alongside it, not merged with it).
codex.hierarchical_behavior: YES - project scope walks from the git root down to cwd, concatenating every matching AGENTS.md/AGENTS.override.md found along the way. Confirmed empirically via `codex debug prompt-input`: a nested subdirectory's own AGENTS.md is appended after the root's content when cwd is inside that subdirectory.
codex.active_entrypoint_selection: EIF's own entrypoint is static per instance (always the project-scope AGENTS.md at the instance root); the ACTIVE SET of files Codex actually merges varies with the cwd a session is run from, which EIF does not control - discovered and dry-run-reported (nested AGENTS.md/AGENTS.override.md files, and same-directory shadow signals), never silently assumed.
codex.shared_vs_dedicated_ownership: shared (entry_ownership=shared) - same contract as CLAUDE.md; AGENTS.md is commonly a file the project already owns.
codex.instruction_size_limit: `project_doc_max_bytes`, default 32 KiB (32,768 bytes) - documented explicitly (developers.openai.com/codex/guides/agents-md); concatenation stops once the combined size reaches this limit, it does not error. EIF does not currently enforce or warn on this limit itself - a residual gap, named not hidden.
codex.headless_runtime_validation: YES - `codex debug prompt-input`, no authentication, no model call, dumps the exact merged prompt input as JSON. Required careful sanitization before recording any evidence, since it also reveals global-scope (personal) content.
codex.package_inclusion: proven from the installed wheel - test_package_build.py's `eifctl init --adapter codex` check, added in Stage 3.

hermes.adapter_switching: supported both directions (claude-code<->hermes); test_hermes_adapter.py scenarios 13/13b/14. A real, previously-crashing edge case found and fixed while building this adapter: CLAUDE.md is both claude-code's own fixed entrypoint AND one of Hermes's own candidates, so switching claude-code -> hermes can land the OLD and NEW entrypoint on the IDENTICAL path - the transaction originally double-staged the same <path>.next file for two separate stages, and the second to commit crashed with 'staged artifact missing'. Fixed in eif_init.py by recognizing the same-path case and skipping the redundant old-entrypoint stage entirely (the entrypoint stage's own marker-merge already replaces the old block with the new one on that single file). Scenario 13b separately proves the genuinely-distinct-path case (switching from Cursor, whose full-regen entrypoint never collides) still deletes the old dedicated file outright as expected.
hermes.runtime_consumption_evidence: CONFIRMED. Verified 2026-07-17 against `hermes --version` (Hermes Agent v0.18.2, 2026.7.7.2, installed via `pip install hermes-agent` from PyPI) and the official docs (hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/context-files): 'Only one project context type is loaded per session (first match wins): .hermes.md -> AGENTS.md -> CLAUDE.md -> .cursorrules.' Real runtime proof via `hermes prompt-size` (offline, no API call - reports byte-count breakdowns, never raw content) against a disposable probe project: confirmed the reported context-tier byte count reflects ONLY the highest-precedence candidate present, never a lower one that also exists; confirmed a root .hermes.md is found from a NESTED cwd (0 bytes became the file's exact byte count once queried from a subdirectory) - the ancestor walk to git root is real; and - the adapter's central limitation - confirmed a root AGENTS.md reports 0 bytes of context when queried from that SAME nested cwd, proving the 'AGENTS.md cwd-only, no parent walk' behavior empirically rather than assuming it from documentation prose. See adapters/hermes/README.md for the full evidence trail. SOUL.md is explicitly out of scope per this round's instruction (a separate mechanism, loaded from HERMES_HOME only, never the working directory).
hermes.instruction_discovery_model: multi-file FIRST-MATCH precedence (not concatenation) across 4 candidate tiers with 2 different discovery scopes - the opposite combination from Codex (which concatenates across an ancestor walk within one scope; Hermes precedence-selects a single file across scopes that differ per candidate).
hermes.precedence: .hermes.md/HERMES.md (tied, undocumented relative order if both exist in the same directory - an open ambiguity, not resolved by assumption) > AGENTS.md > CLAUDE.md > .cursorrules, first match wins, only ONE file loaded total - verbatim from the official docs and confirmed empirically (the higher-precedence file's byte count is reported even when a much-larger lower-precedence file also exists).
hermes.hierarchical_behavior: SPLIT, confirmed empirically: .hermes.md/HERMES.md walk UP from cwd to the git root (closest match wins, capped at 5 parent directories); AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md do NOT walk at all - checked at cwd only. Independently reproduced (a real root AGENTS.md reports 0 bytes of context one level below it; a real root .hermes.md reports its full byte count from that same nested cwd).
hermes.active_entrypoint_selection: DYNAMIC, resolved per-instance by eif_adapters.resolve_dynamic_entrypoint() before every init/upgrade/reconfigure - the only adapter where 'which file is EIF's own entrypoint' is itself computed, not fixed by the registry. The preflight report names exactly which candidate was selected and why (existing-at-root / parent-shadow / default).
hermes.shared_vs_dedicated_ownership: shared (entry_ownership=shared) for whichever candidate is resolved - every one of .hermes.md/HERMES.md/AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md is a plain file a project may already own; there is no dedicated/exclusive Hermes-specific path.
hermes.instruction_size_limit: not documented as a specific byte limit for context files specifically; `hermes prompt-size` reports the full system-prompt budget (~30 KB, including skills index/memory/tool schemas) but names no dedicated cap for the context-file tier the way Codex's `project_doc_max_bytes` does.
hermes.headless_runtime_validation: YES - `hermes prompt-size`, no authentication, no model call, reports byte-count breakdowns by prompt tier. Lower-disclosure-risk than Codex's introspection command by design - never reveals raw content, so no sanitization was needed for any evidence recorded.
hermes.package_inclusion: proven from the installed wheel - test_package_build.py's `eifctl init --adapter hermes` check, added in Stage 4.
